occurrences.opportunityName: Serve Breakfast at the Boston Living Center
occurrences.description:
Victory Programs has helped individuals and families in crisis for 50 years. Nearly 6,000 people turn to us yearly for shelter, sustenance, recovery, care, and professional, compassionate support. The individuals and families we serve across our 25 programs are unhoused or precariously housed, most of whom struggle with substance use, have mental health concerns, and/or live with chronic health issues like HIV/AIDS. When other organizations will not or cannot take them in, we do.



Victory Programs’ Boston Living Center (BLC) is a community and resource center that fosters the wellness of folks living with HIV and other chronic health conditions as well as people experiencing food and housing insecurity. The BLC offers case management, nutritional support, peer services and wellness groups. In an average year, their volunteers help serve over 30,000 meals at the BLC. All meals are designed by a nutritionist, and over 80% of BLC members report the BLC is the first or second source of food.



Help serve breakfast and support morning operations at Victory Programs' beloved Boston Living Center! Please be prepared to help with tasks including checking members in, serving meals, washing dishes, cleaning tables, and other programmatic support. No kitchen experience required. This project can be fast-paced and requires volunteers to stand for the majority of the 3 hour shift. If this is a concern, please contact the Volunteer Leader. Volunteers are required to wear a hat (one will be provided if you do not have one) and closed toed-shoes. Breakfast is served every weekday, and volunteers are asked to be there for the full 3 hour shift to help with set up and cleanup in addition to serving the meal. 



IMPORTANT! Please review the following information before your first time volunteering with Victory Programs:

occurrences.opportunityName: Organize and Distribute Food at Catholic Charities' Yawkey Center Food Pantry
occurrences.description:
For over a century, Catholic Charities Boston has served vulnerable individuals and families of all faiths and backgrounds. One of the most comprehensive non-profit providers of social services in Massachusetts, we offer over 70 programs across more than 20 locations throughout Greater Boston, with 450 employees serving thousands of individuals and families annually within the four core areas of Basic Needs, Family & Youth Services, Refugee & Immigrant Services, and Adult Education & Workforce Development. Rooted in our faith mission, we address critical social justice issues with compassion and aim to break the cycles of poverty in our communities by providing life’s necessities, education, and advocacy to move families toward self-sufficiency.



As a volunteer at Catholic Charities’ Dorchester Food Pantry, your primary role will be to compassionately render distribution of food items to the clients in our pantry, while maintaining person and professional boundaries. This may include restocking pantry shelves, helping with product selection, preparing bags for distribution, client intake, some light cleaning, and helping lift and transport light to moderately-heavy items.



Volunteers will typically be on their feet, and the role does tend to involved bending and lifting (up to 40 lbs). The food pantry serves many Hispanic, Haitian, and Cape Verdean clients, so volunteers with language skills in these areas are highly desired!



IMPORTANT: Catholic Charities Boston asks that all volunteers create an account at https://volunteer.ccab.org/. Please click “sign up” at the top and create an individual volunteer account. Please also register for your shift by responding to the "Boston Cares Volunteers" opportunity (https://volunteer.ccab.org/need/detail/?need_id=1140283) and selecting your shift date(s)/time(s). We also ask that you bring a completed CORI form and a picture ID with you to your first volunteer shift.



MBTA Line Accessibility: The #16 bus stops directly in front of the building. There is a parking lot, but it is not typically open to volunteers, however, there is free street parking on Vaughn Street, which is parallel to Columbia Road.

occurrences.opportunityName: Volunteer at the Hyde Park Emergency Food Pantry
occurrences.description:
Hyde Park Emergency Food Pantry's mission is to provide hunger relief to our neighbors who can't make ends meet. 



Volunteers can do a variety of tasks from: checking clients' IDs checking clients in via our index card system, packing paper/plastic bags of food (frozen, produce, canned goods, etc.), stocking food in refrigerators, freezers, and on shelves, doing light sweeping/wiping down cleaning, and organizing, etc. 



Volunteers will need to stand for the 3-hour session and may need to lift up to 50 lbs. Volunteers who are bilingual in Spanish or Creole are encouraged to sign up!



MBTA Line Accessibility: Commuter Rail on Fairmount, Hyde Park, Readville and buses routes 24, 32, 33, 50
